name: REL6-1-no-previous-release-reads-everything
old:
if (!from) return [];
  const numbers = new Set();
note: With no release before it, the first would read every merge ever made.

name: REL6-2-a-branch-s-own-merges-count
note: A pull request merged into a branch would bring its notes beside the branch's own.

name: REL6-3-a-squash-names-no-pull-request
note: A squash-merged pull request would bring no notes.

name: REL6-4-the-oldest-first
note: The release would open on its oldest change.

name: REL6-5-a-number-twice-is-two
note: A pull request named twice would be read twice.

name: REL6-6-comments-are-notes
note: The template's guidance would be published as the notes.

name: REL6-7-a-fenced-heading-ends-the-notes
note: A "## " line inside a code block would cut the notes short.

name: REL6-8-the-next-section-is-notes
note: The description's next section (## Verification) would be published as notes.

name: REL6-9-headings-kept-a-level-down
note: A ### part would stay ### - a level below the release's own # title.

name: REL6-10-the-footer-is-notes
note: The "Generated with Claude Code" footer and the session link would be published.

name: REL6-11-a-rule-is-notes
note: What stands under a description's rule would be published.

name: REL6-12-headings-alone-are-notes
note: A section of empty headings would be a release of titles.

name: REL6-13-none-is-a-note
note: "None." would be published as the release's notes.

name: REL6-14-the-title-dropped
note: Every release would be titled "Patch Notes".

name: REL6-15-crlf-unread
note: A description written in the browser (CRLF) would bring no notes.

name: REL6-16-a-titled-heading-unread
note: "## Patch notes: <title>", the template's own shape, would bring nothing.

name: REL6-17-never-capped
note: One pull request could fill the release body past GitHub's limit.

name: REL6-18-anyone-s-notes
note: An outside author could edit their merged description into the official release.

name: REL6-19-an-unmerged-pull-request-s-notes
note: A closed, unmerged pull request would bring notes for a change that never shipped.

name: REL6-20-the-repository-ignored
note: A fork's release would read another repository's pull requests.

name: REL6-21-the-newest-last
note: The release would open on its oldest change.

name: REL6-22-a-404-fails-the-release
note: A merge subject naming no pull request here would stop the release.

name: REL6-23-a-failed-read-is-no-notes
note: GitHub down would publish "Fixes and improvements." for a release with notes - for good.

name: REL6-24-the-notes-step-passes-a-failed-read
note: The step would pass with an empty body, and the release publish without notes.

name: REL6-25-the-tag-being-cut-is-its-own-previous
note: Every release would read the merges since itself - none.

name: REL6-26-a-notes-folder-passes
note: A patch-notes FOLDER would pass the tree's guard.

name: REL6-27-the-guard-reads-only-lower-case
note: PATCH-NOTES-*.md - the very files REL6 removed - would pass the guard.

name: REL6-28-the-publish-job-cannot-read-pull-requests
old: pull-requests: read   # REL6: the notes are the merged pull requests' own
note: gh would be refused the pull requests, and every release would fail at its notes.

name: REL6-29-gh-without-its-token
new:
TAG: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}
        run: node scripts/desktopRelease.mjs notes
note: gh would run unauthenticated, and the notes step fail.

name: REL6-30-the-template-asks-for-nothing
note: The template would ask for a section the release never reads.

name: REL6-31-the-template-s-guidance-is-notes
note: A pull request left as the template has it would publish the guidance.
